knowledge_point.title: Applying the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals Over Parametric Curves

question.:question/problem:
Let $f(x,y)=x + y \cos{\left(x \right)}.$ The curve $C$ is parametrized by

$$
\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle t,2 t\right\rangle.
$$

Traverse $C$ from $t=\frac{\pi}{2}$ to $t=\pi.$ Evaluate

$$
\int_C\nabla f\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r.
$$

conversions: evaluate integer powers, exponentials and familiar sin/cos values

question.:question/problem:
Let $f(x,y,z)=2 x y + z.$ The curve $C$ is parametrized by

$$
\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle t,t,t^{2} + 1\right\rangle,\qquad 1\leq t\leq b.
$$

The orientation is given by increasing $t$, and $b>1.$ If

$$
\int_C\nabla f\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=24,
$$

what is $b$?
